findings.reader: A compact, well-bounded research-news article. It answers the availability question first (P001), traces the full causal chain from recorded brain activity through trained decoders to text and avatar output (P002, P003, P005), delivers the study's genuine scientific insight — overlapping signals require combined-context training (P004) — and keeps every limit intact: three participants, two simultaneous users, restricted trained sets, wired lab system, proof of concept not treatment (P005, P006). The closing action (P007) is specific and proportionate. Explain-back and a novel transfer scenario both succeed on the article's stated mechanism. No defect families present.
findings.facts: All nine claims verify against the captured Nature Neuroscience paper and NIH release: three implanted participants attempting trained words and gestures via a motor-cortex ECoG array (P002), parallel decoders driving text and a personalized avatar with two participants using both simultaneously (P003), the overlap/combined-training finding (P004), accurate BCI and decoder definitions with the wired-system and restricted-vocabulary limits (P005), and the proof-of-concept, further-testing framing (P006). No overstatement, no dropped attribution, no stale or unreviewable claim; factual integrity, freshness, dated-change handling and uncertainty preservation all pass.
